title: Asymmetric shard scheduling experiment log
content:
Summary:
This doc captures an exploratory run of asymmetric shard scheduling and related microbenchmarks to understand whether intentionally uneven tensor/pipeline shard assignment can improve tail latency and throughput for models with non-uniform layer compute costs. Unlike prior topology/NCCl saturation explorations, we focused on: 1) layer-level compute imbalance (e.g., FOFE/Flash-attention fused layers), 2) placement heuristics that assign heavier layers fewer parallel copies, and 3) the interaction with NCCL communicator construction when links are asymmetric (NVLink chain + PCIe fallback).

Goals / hypotheses:
- H1: For models whose layers vary 2x+ in FLOPs, symmetric TP sharding yields GPU idling and reduces throughput; asymmetric shard assignment can reduce idle time and improve throughput by 5-20% in some cases.
- H2: When NVLink rings are asymmetric (mixed NVLink+PCIe hops), naive allreduce patterns cause hot links. Explicit communicator grouping + NCCL tuning mitigates link hot-spotting.
- H3: Pipeline-parallel microbatching interacts with asymmetric tensor shards; need combined scheduler to avoid head-of-line stalls.

Testbed:
- Cluster: 4x A100-SXM-40GB on single node (nvlink fully connected) + multi-node runs on 2 nodes x 4x A100 with mixed NVLink topology (rack switch).
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04, CUDA 11.8, cuBLAS 11.10, NCCL 2.14.3, libcudnn 8.2.
- Tools: nsys (NVIDIA Nsight Systems), nvprof for micro kernels, nvlink-topology viewer, nccl-tests (allreduce_perf), ib_send_bw for RDMA checks, nvidia-smi dmon, gpustat, bpftrace for CPU-side blocking traces.
- Models tested: small baseline (6B transformer) and wide model (70B transformer-like with a handful of fused attention blocks). Sequence length: 512 and 2048. Microbatch sizes: 1, 2, 4. TP degrees: 1, 2, 4. PP degrees: 1, 2.

Experiment 1 — layer-cost-aware TP split (single node, 4 GPUs):
- Approach: Compute per-layer execution time profile using nsys sampling on a single-GPU run to get relative cost per transformer layer. Create a simple greedy partitioner that assigns contiguous layer ranges to GPUs but balances total FLOP-time instead of layer count.
- Configs: symmetric (equal layer counts) vs asymmetric (greedy time-balanced). No pipeline parallelism.
- Observed (6B, seq512, batch1):
  - Symmetric TP (2-way): throughput 420 tokens/s, p99 token latency 35ms, GPU utilization (avg) ~72% (one GPU peaked 94%, one at 50%).
  - Asymmetric TP (2-way time-balanced): throughput 475 tokens/s (+13%), p99 31ms (-11%), utilization ~85% across GPUs (peaks closer).
- Observed (70B, seq512, batch1, TP=4):
  - Symmetric: throughput 120 tokens/s, p99 110ms, pronounced stalling on GPUs 2 and 3.
  - Asymmetric: throughput 140 tokens/s (+17%), p99 95ms (-13%).
- Notes: improvement biggest when per-layer cost variance >1.7x. For models with highly uniform layers (no fused ops), improvements were <3% and sometimes negative due to increased communication imbalance.

Experiment 2 — NCCL communicator grouping to avoid hot NVLink chains (multi-node mixed links):
- Problem: allreduce across 8 GPUs produced consistent saturation on single NVLink chain; other links underutilized. Observed high error rates and retries (nccl debug logs).
- Approach: build communicators that prefer NVLink-connected cliques and fall back to inter-node bridges for cross-clique reductions (hierarchical allreduce). Use NCCL_COLLECTIVES=1 and set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to restrict network interfaces during multi-node runs.
- Configs: default NCCL vs hierarchical grouping with explicit process-group ordering (we used custom rendezvous to form intra-host communicators first).
- Observed: hierarchical grouping reduced peak NVLink utilization (~30% reduction on top chain) and lowered p99 by ~9% for the 70B TP=4 case. End-to-end throughput improved by ~11%.
- NCCL env tweaks that helped in our runs: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0, NCCL_IB_GDR_LEVEL=2 (when using GPUDirect RDMA across nodes), NCCL_ALGO=RING for small payloads but TREE/RING-SPLIT for larger collective sizes.

Experiment 3 — pipeline + asymmetric shards (interleaved vs contiguous pipeline schedules):
- Setup: PP degree 2 + TP degree 2 (total 4 GPUs), run microbatching with different interleaving schedules.
- Observation: When asymmetric TP assigned more compute-heavy layers to GPU0 (early), the pipeline head would finish later and stall downstream GPUs waiting on activations, causing serialization.
- Fixes tested: 1) adjust microbatch size to increase in-flight microbatches (reduces head-of-line effect), 2) reorder pipeline chunks to balance forward/backward work (interleaved pipeline layout), 3) slight overprovisioning of TP capacity for heavy shards (reserve an idle-buffer slot).
- Results: best result was interleaved PP layout + 2 microbatches which matched asymmetric TP gains while avoiding stalls; throughput improved ~9% vs symmetric baseline at PP=2, TP=2 for 6B model.

Profiling notes and artifacts:
- nsys traces show long gaps between kernel launches on GPUs that had tiny shard assignments (sign of imbalance).
- nsight report attached to PR shows cudaMemcpyPeer activity sharply spiking on one NVLink pair at the start of the forward pass in symmetric shards for 70B.
- nccl-tests (allreduce_perf) measured per-link bandwidth and showed sustained bw on one NVLink pair at 90% while adjacent link pairs idle at 20%. Indicates suboptimal ring formation by default NCCL on our topology.

Key commands/ snippets used (for reproducibility):
- Run profiling: nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas,nccl -o trace.nsys python serving_run.py --config cfg.yaml
- Inspect NCCL runtime: export NCCL_DEBUG=WARN; export NCCL_TOPO_DUMP_FILE=/tmp/nccl_topo.json; run workload
- Force hierarchical: python launcher.py --group-intra-host --comm-hierarchy intra,inter --tp 2 --pp 2 --model 70B
- Greedy partitioner (pseudo): python partitioner.py --layer-times layer_times.json --gpus 4 --mode greedy_time_balance

Quantitative summary (representative):
- 6B model, single-node 4gpus, TP=2: symmetric 420 t/s -> asymmetric 475 t/s (+13%).
- 70B model, 2 nodes x 4gpus, TP=4: symmetric 120 t/s -> asymmetric + hierarchical NCCL 140 t/s (+17% throughput).
- p99 reduced by 9-15% for best configs above.

Failure modes and caveats:
- Communication imbalance can worsen if layer assignment creates larger cross-GPU activation transfers; partitioner must incorporate activation size and not just compute time.
- For extremely memory-bound layers (attention with long context), asymmetric assignments may cause OOM on heavy-GPU even if compute balanced. Must add free-memory constraint in scheduler.
- NCCL version-dependent: observed different ring selection behavior between NCCL 2.12 and 2.14; retest before rolling out changes to managed clusters.

Recommendations and short-term action items:
1) Add layer-wise activation-size measurement to partitioner so it balances both compute and communication (owner: Rafael, ETA: 2w).
2) Prototype communicator hierarchy in serving runtime: prefer intra-host clique reductions then inter-host bridges; add as an opt-in config. (owner: Priya, ETA: 3w).
3) Bake a sanity-checker that simulates per-step memory usage for candidate partitions to avoid OOMs (owner: Noah, ETA: 1w).
4) Run a wider sweep across model types (MoE, fused-attention) and larger clusters (8+ GPUs) before any scheduling policy defaults are changed (owner: Evelyn, ETA: 6w).

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- How does asymmetric scheduling interact with NVSwitch topologies vs NVLink daisy chains? Need microbenchmarks capturing ring vs tree topologies.
- Can we auto-detect when asymmetric scheduling will help (threshold of per-layer variance)? Build simple heuristic based on coefficient of variation of layer times.
- Explore dynamic re-sharding during long-running sessions (migrate heavy layers to underutilized GPUs during slack periods).

Relevant links and traces:
- Quick profile gist: https://gist.github.com/evelynz/abc123 (contains sample nsys flame graphs)
- PR with prototype partitioner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482
- JIRA ticket for follow-up sweep: INF-1245

Notes to reviewers:
- This log is intentionally lightweight and experimental: many knobs were manually tweaked. The goal is to capture signal for productizing "time- and comm-aware shard placement" rather than to propose final defaults.
- Please focus review on heuristics we used to compute layer time (nsys wall-time sampling with 10 warmup iterations) and the safety checks (memory & activation constraints).

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducing main asymmetric run
- Setup same CUDA / NCCL versions as top of doc.
- Collect per-layer times: run single-GPU trace for N=50 iterations, average layer times after removing first 10 warmups.
- Run partitioner with compute+activation weights: partitioner.py --compute-times layer_times.json --activation-sizes act_sizes.json --gpus 4 --balance compute+comm --out plan.json
- Launch with hierarchical NCCL: launcher.py --plan plan.json --nccl-hierarchy intra-first --tp 4 --pp 1

End of doc.
